claim: The Drosophila wing disc is composed of epithelial cells that form a sac-like structure comprising the columnar cells of the disc proper and the squamous cells of the peripodial epithelium.
source: The wing-imaginal disc is composed of epithelial cells that form a sac-like structure (comprising the columnar cells of the disc proper and the squamous cells of the peripodial epithelium [PE]) and a population of adult muscle precursors (AMPs) that resides between the epithelial cells of the disc proper and the underlying basement membrane (Figure 1A).
evidence: This is a direct statement in the manuscript describing the cellular composition of the wing disc.

claim: Adult muscle precursors (AMPs) reside between the epithelial cells of the disc proper and the underlying basement membrane.
source: The wing-imaginal disc is composed of epithelial cells that form a sac-like structure (comprising the columnar cells of the disc proper and the squamous cells of the peripodial epithelium [PE]) and a population of adult muscle precursors (AMPs) that resides between the epithelial cells of the disc proper and the underlying basement membrane (Figure 1A).
evidence: This is a direct statement describing the location of AMPs in the wing disc.

claim: The epithelial portion of the disc derives from a primordium of approximately 30 cells from the embryonic ectoderm that are specified during embryogenesis.
source: The epithelial portion of the disc derives from a primordium of approximately 30 cells from the embryonic ectoderm that are specified during embryogenesis (Mandaravally Madhavan and Schneiderman, 1977; Worley et al., 2013; Requena et al., 2017).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to previous research.

claim: The AMPs represent a subset of cells from the embryonic mesoderm that generate the adult flight muscles.
source: The AMPs, originally referred to as adepithelial cells (Poodry and Schneiderman, 1970), represent a subset of cells from the embryonic mesoderm that generate the adult flight muscles (Bate et al., 1991; Fernandes et al., 1991).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to previous research.

claim: The AMPs underlie the dorsal portion of the wing disc epithelium, the notum, which is the primordium of the dorsal thorax.
source: The AMPs underlie the dorsal portion of the wing disc epithelium, the notum, which is the primordium of the dorsal thorax.
evidence: This is a direct statement describing the location of AMPs relative to the notum.

claim: During metamorphosis, AMPs generate multiple muscle fibers that comprise the direct and indirect flight muscles (DFMs and IFMs, respectively).
source: During metamorphosis, these AMPs generate multiple muscle fibers that comprise the direct and indirect flight muscles (DFMs and IFMs, respectively) (reviewed by Bothe and Baylies, 2016; Gunage et al., 2017; Laurichesse and Soler, 2020).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to review articles.

claim: Single-cell transcriptomics data were collected from wing discs at mid and late third instar, corresponding to 96 and 120 hr after egg lay (AEL).
source: With the goal of generating a spatiotemporal atlas of the developing wing disc, we used single-cell RNA sequencing to collect transcriptional profiles of cells at mid and late third instar, which correspond to 96 and 120 hr after egg lay (AEL) (Figure 1A).
evidence: This is a direct statement describing the experimental design.

claim: Two biological replicates were obtained at each time point, generating data from 6922 and 7091 cells in the 96 hr samples and 7453 and 5550 cells in the 120 hr samples after filtering for low-quality cells.
source: Two biological replicates were obtained at each time point that, after filtering for low-quality cells, generated data from 6922 and 7091 cells in the 96 hr samples and 7453 and 5550 cells in the 120 hr samples.
evidence: This is a direct statement describing the number of cells analyzed.

claim: Harmonization of the different samples and dimensionality reduction was performed using scVI.
source: Harmonization of the different samples and dimensionality reduction was performed using scVI (Lopez et al., 2018).
evidence: This statement describes the computational method used and cites the relevant publication.

claim: Clustering and differential expression analysis was done with the Seurat v3 R package.
source: Clustering and differential expression analysis was done with the Seurat v3 R package (Stuart et al., 2019), and two-dimensional visualization of the data was performed with Uniform Manifold Approximation and Projection (UMAP) (McInnes et al., 2018) (see Materials and methods).
evidence: This statement describes the computational method used and cites the relevant publication.

claim: Two-dimensional visualization of the data was performed with Uniform Manifold Approximation and Projection (UMAP).
source: Clustering and differential expression analysis was done with the Seurat v3 R package (Stuart et al., 2019), and two-dimensional visualization of the data was performed with Uniform Manifold Approximation and Projection (UMAP) (McInnes et al., 2018) (see Materials and methods).
evidence: This statement describes the computational method used and cites the relevant publication.

claim: The single-cell analysis identified four major cell types: the AMPs, the wing disc epithelial cells (disc proper and PE), tracheal cells, and hemocytes.
source: Our single-cell analysis identified four major cell types via known gene markers (Figure 1B–E, Figure 1—figure supplement 1A–G): the AMPs, the wing disc epithelial cells (disc proper and PE), and small numbers of tracheal cells and hemocytes.
evidence: This statement is supported by reference to figures showing the identification of cell types.

claim: A similar set of marker genes was observed in each of these cell types to those described by others.
source: We observed expression of a similar set of marker genes in each of these cell types to those described by others (Deng et al., 2019; Bageritz et al., 2019; Zappia et al., 2020).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to previous research.

claim: The dataset shows an overrepresentation of AMPs, probably the result of the collagenase-based dissociation protocol that dissociated AMPs far more effectively than epithelial cells.
source: Notably, our dataset shows an overrepresentation of AMPs, probably the result of our collagenase-based dissociation protocol (see Materials and methods) that dissociated AMPs far more effectively than epithelial cells.
evidence: This statement provides an inference about the cause of the overrepresentation based on the dissociation method.

claim: Profiles for 19,885 AMPs, 7104 wing disc epithelial cells, 15 tracheal cells, and 12 hemocytes were recovered.
source: Altogether, we recovered profiles for 19,885 AMPs, 7104 wing disc epithelial cells, 15 tracheal cells, and 12 hemocytes.
evidence: This is a direct statement describing the number of cells of each type recovered.

claim: Expression changes between 96 and 120 hr that occurred in both the epithelium and the AMPs together, as well as those changes that were confined to either the epithelial cells or the AMPs, were observed.
source: Unlike bulk RNA-sequencing approaches that would average changes in gene expression across multiple cell types, we were able to observe expression changes between 96 and 120 hr that occurred in both the epithelium and the AMPs together, as well as those changes that were confined to either the epithelial cells or the AMPs (Figure 1—figure supplement 1H and Supplementary file 1).
evidence: This statement is supported by reference to a figure and supplementary file.

claim: The wing disc epithelium is often divided into four broad domains – the notum, hinge, pouch, and PE – based both on morphology and gene expression patterns.
source: The wing disc epithelium is often divided into four broad domains – the notum, hinge, pouch, and PE – based both on morphology and gene expression patterns.
evidence: This is a statement of established knowledge about the wing disc.

claim: The genes encoding the transcription factors nubbin (nub) and Zn finger homeodomain 2 (zfh2) were used to define the pouch and hinge, respectively.
source: The genes encoding the transcription factors nubbin (nub) and Zn finger homeodomain 2 (zfh2) were used to define the pouch and hinge, respectively (Zirin and Mann, 2007; Terriente et al., 2008; Ayala-Camargo et al., 2013).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to previous research.

claim: Epithelial cells were clustered and then classified as originating from the larger domains of notum, hinge, pouch, and PE based on the expression patterns of marker genes.
source: To characterize the epithelial compartment, we clustered the cells and then classified these clusters as originating from the larger domains of notum, hinge, pouch, and PE based on the expression patterns of marker genes (Figure 1H–K, Figure 1—figure supplement 2A).
evidence: This statement describes the analysis method and is supported by reference to figures.

claim: Many marker genes were already expressed in a domain-specific manner by 96 hr, suggesting that cells in the epithelium had already been partitioned into these domains.
source: Many of these genes were already expressed in a domain-specific manner by 96 hr, suggesting that cells in the epithelium had already been partitioned into these domains (Figure 1I–K, Figure 1—figure supplement 2B).
evidence: This statement is an inference based on the observed gene expression patterns shown in figures.

claim: The proximodistal axis was a primary feature in stratifying cells within the analysis, while the anteroposterior axis separated the data to a lesser degree.
source: The proximodistal axis was a primary feature in stratifying cells within our analysis, while the anteroposterior axis separated the data to a lesser degree.
evidence: This is a direct statement describing the results of the analysis.

claim: Anterior and posterior cells arise from distinct embryonic subpopulations.
source: This is somewhat surprising because anterior and posterior cells arise from distinct embryonic subpopulations (Garcia-Bellido et al., 1973; Mandaravally Madhavan and Schneiderman, 1977; Worley et al., 2013; Requena et al., 2017).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to previous research.

claim: Cells were classified as anterior or posterior cells based on expression of compartment marker genes (e.g., cubitus interruptus, hedgehog, and engrailed).
source: We classified cells as anterior or posterior cells based on expression of compartment marker genes (e.g., cubitus interruptus, hedgehog, and engrailed) (Figure 1—figure supplement 3A–E) and found that the concise representation of the data in two dimensions (with UMAP) resulted in stratification of the cells based on the proximodistal axis first, with secondary stratification of cells based on anteroposterior identity (Figure 1—figure supplement 3E).
evidence: This statement describes the analysis method and is supported by reference to figures.

claim: The concise representation of the data in two dimensions (with UMAP) resulted in stratification of the cells based on the proximodistal axis first, with secondary stratification of cells based on anteroposterior identity.
source: We classified cells as anterior or posterior cells based on expression of compartment marker genes (e.g., cubitus interruptus, hedgehog, and engrailed) (Figure 1—figure supplement 3A–E) and found that the concise representation of the data in two dimensions (with UMAP) resulted in stratification of the cells based on the proximodistal axis first, with secondary stratification of cells based on anteroposterior identity (Figure 1—figure supplement 3E).
evidence: This statement describes the results of the analysis and is supported by reference to a figure.

claim: There are more differentially expressed genes across the proximodistal axis than the anteroposterior axis.
source: Additional analysis indicated that there are more differentially expressed genes across the proximodistal axis than the anteroposterior axis (Figure 1—figure supplement 3F–H).
evidence: This statement describes the results of the analysis and is supported by reference to a figure.

claim: 337 and 408 genes were significantly downregulated and upregulated, respectively, within at least one cluster between 96 and 120 hr AEL.
source: To investigate how cells changed over developmental time, we analyzed transcriptional changes that occurred within epithelium cell clusters between 96 and 120 hr AEL and found that 337 and 408 genes were significantly downregulated and upregulated, respectively, within at least one cluster (see Materials and methods; Figure 1—figure supplement 2C; Supplementary file 2).
evidence: This statement describes the results of the analysis and is supported by reference to a figure and supplementary file.

claim: string (stg), which encodes a regulator of the cell cycle, is upregulated within the wing margin while being downregulated in other regions of the disc.
source: One example is string (stg) (Edgar and O'Farrell, 1990), which encodes a regulator of the cell cycle and is upregulated within the wing margin while being downregulated in other regions of the disc.
evidence: This statement describes a specific example of gene expression changes and cites the relevant publication.

claim: Even though the major cell types are established by 96 hr of development, there is evidence of further pattern refinement via highly localized gene expression changes.
source: Thus, even though the major cell types are established by 96 hr of development (Figure 1I–K, Figure 1—figure supplement 2B), we still find evidence of further pattern refinement via highly localized gene expression changes (Figure 1—figure supplement 2C).
evidence: This statement is an inference based on the observed gene expression patterns shown in figures.

claim: Initial analysis of the AMPs showed a clear partition of the cells with respect to two primary features: cell sex (discs were collected from both male and female larvae) and cell cycle phase.
source: Initial analysis of the AMPs showed a clear partition of the cells with respect to two primary features: cell sex (discs were collected from both male and female larvae) and cell cycle phase (Figure 1—figure supplement 4A–G, Figure 1—figure supplement 5A–G).
evidence: This statement describes the results of the analysis and is supported by reference to figures.

claim: scVI was utilized to suppress the effects of cell sex and cell cycle phase covariates, which enabled a clearer view of other aspects of AMP cell biology.
source: We utilized scVI to suppress the effects of these covariates, which enabled us to obtain a clearer view of other aspects of AMP cell biology (see Materials and methods).
evidence: This statement describes the computational method used.

claim: The AMPs are known to differentiate into either DFMs or IFMs of the adult fly.
source: The AMPs are known to differentiate into either DFMs or IFMs of the adult fly (Bate, 1993; Roy and VijayRaghavan, 1999; Sudarsan et al., 2001).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to previous research.

claim: The precursors of DFMs and IFMs can be identified by their location within the tissue and are canonically classified by their relative expression of two transcription factors, Vg and Ct, at the late third instar larval (L3) stage (corresponding to the 120 hr time point).
source: The precursors of these two populations can be identified by their location within the tissue and are canonically classified by their relative expression of two transcription factors, Vg and Ct, at the late third instar larval (L3) stage (corresponding to our 120 hr time point) (Sudarsan et al., 2001).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to previous research.

claim: The precursor cells of the IFMs are localized more dorsally (closer to the wing disc stalk) and display relatively high Vg and low Ct protein expression.
source: The precursor cells of the IFMs are localized more dorsally (closer to the wing disc stalk) and display relatively high Vg and low Ct protein expression (Sudarsan et al., 2001).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to previous research.

claim: The DFM cell precursors are localized more ventrally (closer to the wing hinge) and are identifiable by little or no Vg and high Ct protein expression.
source: The DFM cell precursors are localized more ventrally (closer to the wing hinge) and are identifiable by little or no Vg and high Ct protein expression (Sudarsan et al., 2001).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to previous research.

claim: After unsupervised clustering, one cluster was characterized by high levels of ct and low levels of vg, and the remaining clusters displayed relatively elevated levels of vg and low levels of ct.
source: After unsupervised clustering (Figure 1N), we found that one cluster was characterized by high levels of ct and low levels of vg, and the remaining clusters displayed relatively elevated levels of vg and low levels of ct (Figure 1O–Q, Figure 1—figure supplement 5E, F).
evidence: This statement describes the results of the analysis and is supported by reference to figures.

claim: Based on the distinction in ct and vg expression, cells were classified as representing the direct or indirect AMPs, obtaining 17,604 indirect AMPs and 2281 direct AMPs.
source: Based on this distinction, we classified cells as representing the direct or indirect AMPs (Figure 1N, Figure 1—figure supplement 5F), obtaining 17,604 indirect AMPs and 2281 direct AMPs.
evidence: This statement describes the results of the analysis and is supported by reference to figures.

claim: Although the expression of ct and vg was less distinct at 96 hr, the analysis still classified cells from 96 hr into both direct and indirect populations.
source: Although the expression of ct and vg was less distinct at 96 hr, our analysis still classified cells from 96 hr into both direct and indirect populations.
evidence: This statement describes the results of the analysis.

claim: A small number of genes showed differential expression between direct and indirect AMPs at both time points, possibly indicative of pathways that are necessary both for the initial establishment and subsequent maintenance of AMP cell types.
source: We identified a small number of genes that at both time points showed differential expression between direct and indirect AMPs (Figure 1—figure supplement 6A; Supplementary file 3), possibly indicative of pathways that are necessary both for the initial establishment and subsequent maintenance of AMP cell types.
evidence: This statement is an inference based on the observed gene expression patterns shown in figures.

claim: Genes showing differential expression between direct and indirect AMPs at both time points included several predicted targets of Wg signaling, specifically naked cuticle (nkd) and vg, and the modulator of Notch signaling fringe (fng).
source: This included several predicted targets of Wg signaling, specifically naked cuticle (nkd) and vg, and the modulator of Notch signaling fringe (fng) (Figure 1—figure supplement 6A, B).
evidence: This statement describes specific genes identified in the analysis and is supported by reference to figures.

claim: The majority of differentially expressed genes between direct and indirect AMPs were developmentally regulated, with differential expression only observed at 120 hr.
source: However, the majority of differentially expressed genes that we identified were developmentally regulated. For these genes, differential expression between the direct and indirect AMPs was only observed at 120 hr.
evidence: This statement describes the results of the analysis.

claim: Unlike the epithelium, the subdivision of the AMPs into direct and indirect pools (as assessed by differential expression of genes) mostly occurs only by 120 hr.
source: Thus, unlike the epithelium, the subdivision of the AMPs into direct and indirect pools (as assessed by differential expression of genes) mostly occurs only by 120 hr.
evidence: This statement is an inference based on the observed gene expression patterns.

claim: From 96 to 120 hr, the activation and refinement of expression of many genes previously implicated in axon guidance was observed.
source: From 96 to 120 hr, we noticed the activation and refinement of expression of many genes previously implicated in axon guidance (Figure 1—figure supplement 6A).
evidence: This statement describes the results of the analysis and is supported by reference to a figure.

claim: Genes previously implicated in axon guidance include the receptor–ligand pairs roundabout2/slit and Neurotactin/Amalgam, as well as the synaptic partner-matching genes Ten-a and Ten-m.
source: These include the receptor–ligand pairs roundabout2/slit and Neurotactin/Amalgam (Kidd et al., 1999; Frémion et al., 2000), as well as the synaptic partner-matching genes Ten-a and Ten-m (Hong et al., 2012).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to previous research.

claim: Ten-m protein increases in expression from 96 to 120 hr, as confirmed by staining discs with anti-Ten-m antibody.
source: We confirmed that Ten-m protein increases in expression from 96 to 120 hr by staining discs with anti-Ten-m antibody (Figure 1—figure supplement 6C).
evidence: This statement describes the results of an experiment and is supported by reference to a figure.

claim: Pathways known to function in axon guidance could also function in myoblasts.
source: These observations suggest that pathways known to function in axon guidance could also function in myoblasts.
evidence: This statement is a speculation based on the observed gene expression patterns.

claim: A three-layered model was generated, with gene expression levels inferred at different spatial positions within the AMP, disc proper, and PE layers.
source: First, to predict and visualize the location of gene expression within the wing disc, we generated a three-layered model, with gene expression levels inferred at different spatial positions within the AMP, disc proper, and PE layers.
evidence: This statement describes the computational method used.

claim: The three-layered model enabled the discovery of the expression of genes in regions of the disc epithelium that are closest to the AMPs as well as in the AMPs themselves.
source: This enabled us to discover the expression of genes in regions of the disc epithelium that are closest to the AMPs as well as in the AMPs themselves.
evidence: This statement describes the utility of the computational method.

claim: The expression of ligand–receptor pairs was examined to identify those with complementary expression patterns between the disc epithelium and the AMPs.
source: Second, we examined the expression of ligand–receptor pairs to identify those with complementary expression patterns between the disc epithelium and the AMPs.
evidence: This statement describes the analysis method.

claim: Cells were mapped with the R package DistMap, and the reference model was assembled from a manually curated set of gene expression patterns.
source: The cells were mapped with the R package DistMap (Karaiskos et al., 2017), and the reference model was assembled from a manually curated set of gene expression patterns (Figure 2A and Materials and methods).
evidence: This statement describes the computational method used and cites the relevant publication.

claim: The spatial mapping of cells was largely consistent with manual cluster annotations based on marker genes.
source: This spatial mapping of cells was largely consistent with our manual cluster annotations based on marker genes (Figure 2—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This statement describes the results of the analysis and is supported by reference to a figure.

claim: The spatial mapping was consistent with the four broad epithelial domains (notum, hinge, pouch, PE) and more refined cell groups, such as the wing margin, posterior notum, outer pouch, and anterior hinge.
source: This included the four broad epithelial domains (notum, hinge, pouch, PE; Figure 2B) and more refined cell groups, such as the wing margin, posterior notum, outer pouch, and anterior hinge (Figure 2C).
evidence: This statement describes the results of the analysis and is supported by reference to figures.

claim: The predicted patterns of grain (grn) and pou domain motif 3 (pdm3) largely matched the expressions of transcriptional reporters for grn and pdm3 within wing discs.
source: To test how well our virtual wing disc would predict novel gene expression patterns, we predicted the virtual in situ expression patterns of grain (grn) and pou domain motif 3 (pdm3), neither of which were included in generating the disc model. The predicted patterns largely matched the expressions of transcriptional reporters for grn and pdm3 within wing discs (Figure 2D–G), indicating that our virtual wing disc can successfully predict novel gene expression patterns.
evidence: This statement describes the results of a validation experiment and is supported by reference to figures.

claim: The virtual wing disc can successfully predict novel gene expression patterns.
source: The predicted patterns largely matched the expressions of transcriptional reporters for grn and pdm3 within wing discs (Figure 2D–G), indicating that our virtual wing disc can successfully predict novel gene expression patterns.
evidence: This statement is an inference based on the validation experiment.

claim: High levels of expression of the genes encoding two FGF-family ligands, thisbe (ths) and pyramus (pyr), were observed in the notum region of the epithelium.
source: Interestingly, we observed high levels of expression of the genes encoding two FGF-family ligands, thisbe (ths) and pyramus (pyr) (Stathopoulos et al., 2004), in the notum region of the epithelium, whereas the gene encoding their receptor, heartless (htl) (Beiman et al., 1996), was specifically expressed in the AMPs.
evidence: This statement describes the results of the analysis and cites relevant publications.

claim: The gene encoding the FGF receptor heartless (htl) was specifically expressed in the AMPs.
source: Interestingly, we observed high levels of expression of the genes encoding two FGF-family ligands, thisbe (ths) and pyramus (pyr) (Stathopoulos et al., 2004), in the notum region of the epithelium, whereas the gene encoding their receptor, heartless (htl) (Beiman et al., 1996), was specifically expressed in the AMPs.
evidence: This statement describes the results of the analysis and cites relevant publications.

claim: The ligand hedgehog (hh) appears to be expressed only in the disc epithelium.
source: Similarly, the ligand hedgehog (hh) appears to be expressed only in the disc epithelium, while its receptor patched (ptc) and signal transducer smoothened (smo) are both expressed in the epithelium as expected, but also unexpectedly in the AMPs.
evidence: This statement describes the results of the analysis.

claim: The Hedgehog receptor patched (ptc) and signal transducer smoothened (smo) are both expressed in the epithelium as expected, but also unexpectedly in the AMPs.
source: Similarly, the ligand hedgehog (hh) appears to be expressed only in the disc epithelium, while its receptor patched (ptc) and signal transducer smoothened (smo) are both expressed in the epithelium as expected, but also unexpectedly in the AMPs.
evidence: This statement describes the results of the analysis.

claim: Ths and Pyr are the ligands for one of the Drosophila FGF signaling pathways, and both interact with the receptor Htl.
source: Ths and Pyr are the ligands for one of the Drosophila FGF signaling pathways, and both interact with the receptor Htl (Stathopoulos et al., 2004; Figure 3A).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to previous research and reference to a figure.

claim: htl is detected in nearly all of the AMPs.
source: While htl is detected in nearly all of the AMPs, the three-layered disc map predicts that ths and pyr are expressed primarily in the epithelial cells of the notum, with considerable overlap (Figure 3B–D).
evidence: This statement describes the results of the analysis and is supported by reference to figures.

claim: The three-layered disc map predicts that ths and pyr are expressed primarily in the epithelial cells of the notum, with considerable overlap.
source: While htl is detected in nearly all of the AMPs, the three-layered disc map predicts that ths and pyr are expressed primarily in the epithelial cells of the notum, with considerable overlap (Figure 3B–D).
evidence: This statement describes the results of the analysis and is supported by reference to figures.

claim: ths is localized to the most proximal region of the notum, while pyr has a broader expression pattern extending into the posterior hinge.
source: Specifically, ths is localized to the most proximal region of the notum, while pyr has a broader expression pattern extending into the posterior hinge (compare Figure 3C and D).
evidence: This statement describes the results of the analysis and is supported by reference to figures.

claim: The expression patterns of ths and htl reporters were consistent with the expression predicted using the virtual wing disc.
source: The expression patterns of ths and htl reporters were consistent with the expression predicted using our virtual wing disc (Figure 3E, I).
evidence: This statement describes the results of a validation experiment and is supported by reference to figures.

claim: During embryogenesis, htl, ths, and pyr are known to influence mesoderm spreading along the embryonic ectoderm and formation of cardiac progenitor cells.
source: During embryogenesis, htl, ths, and pyr are known to influence mesoderm spreading along the embryonic ectoderm and formation of cardiac progenitor cells (Beiman et al., 1996; Stathopoulos et al., 2004; Kadam et al., 2009).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to previous research.

claim: In htl mutants and in ths and pyr double mutants, mesoderm cells are still present within the embryo, but they accumulate in multilayered arrangements instead of a monolayer along the ectoderm (as observed in wild-type embryos).
source: Notably, in htl mutants and in ths and pyr double mutants, mesoderm cells are still present within the embryo, but they accumulate in multilayered arrangements instead of a monolayer along the ectoderm (as observed in wild-type embryos) (Beiman et al., 1996; Stathopoulos et al., 2004; Kadam et al., 2009).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to previous research.

claim: FGF signaling might be primarily needed for proper mesoderm spreading rather than for cell proliferation and survival.
source: These observations suggest that FGF signaling might be primarily needed for proper mesoderm spreading rather than for cell proliferation and survival.
evidence: This statement is a speculation based on observations from previous research.

claim: Ths and Pyr may regulate the localization of AMPs relative to the epithelium.
source: By analogy, Ths and Pyr may regulate the localization of AMPs relative to the epithelium.
evidence: This statement is a speculation based on analogy to embryonic development.

claim: Expressing an RNAi that targets pyr with the ap-Gal4 driver resulted in a reduction in AMPs and an obvious increase in apoptosis (visualized using anti-Dcp1), primarily observed in the more ventral- and posterior-localized AMPs.
source: Expressing an RNAi that targets pyr with this ap-Gal4 driver resulted in a reduction in AMPs and an obvious increase in apoptosis (visualized using anti-Dcp1), primarily observed in the more ventral- and posterior-localized AMPs (Figure 3H, compare with Figure 3F).
evidence: This statement describes the results of an experiment and is supported by reference to figures.

claim: pyr knockdown within the wing disc restricts AMP survival to the Ths-expressing region of the dorsal notum as Pyr and Ths have been noted to have partially redundant functions.
source: A likely explanation for this result is that pyr knockdown within the wing disc restricts AMP survival to the Ths-expressing region of the dorsal notum as Pyr and Ths have been noted to have partially redundant functions (Stathopoulos et al., 2004; Kadam et al., 2009).
evidence: This statement is an inference based on the experimental results and cites relevant publications.

claim: Sufficient Ths cannot reach the ventral and posterior region of the notum to compensate for the knockdown of Pyr at physiological levels of Ths expression.
source: Moreover, this result suggests that sufficient Ths cannot reach this region of the notum to compensate for the knockdown of Pyr at physiological levels of Ths expression.
evidence: This statement is an inference based on the experimental results.

claim: Using the AMP-specific driver 15B03-Gal4, expression of an RNAi for htl resulted in an obvious decrease in the number of AMPs following knockdown of FGF signal transduction.
source: Using the AMP-specific driver 15B03-Gal4 (Figure 3J), we expressed an RNAi for htl and observed an obvious decrease in the number of AMPs following knockdown of FGF signal transduction (Figure 3K).
evidence: This statement describes the results of an experiment and is supported by reference to figures.

claim: FGF signaling between AMPs and the disc epithelium is necessary for proper AMP survival.
source: Altogether, we conclude that FGF signaling between AMPs and the disc epithelium is necessary for proper AMP survival.
evidence: This statement is a conclusion based on the experimental results.

claim: Expression of either pyr or ths in the dpp-Gal4 domain caused a massive increase in the number of AMPs, not only beneath the notum epithelium where AMPs are normally present, but throughout the entire dpp-Gal4 expression domain, including underneath the wing pouch.
source: Expression of either pyr or ths in this domain caused a massive increase in the number of AMPs, not only beneath the notum epithelium where AMPs are normally present, but throughout the entire dpp-Gal4 expression domain, including underneath the wing pouch (Figure 4B, Figure 4—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: This statement describes the results of an experiment and is supported by reference to figures.

claim: AMPs were observed along the entire stripe of ectopic FGF expression, all the way to the ventral hinge and even extending on the ventral side to the peripodial epithelium.
source: AMPs were observed along the entire stripe of ectopic FGF expression, all the way to the ventral hinge and even extending on the ventral side to the peripodial epithelium.
evidence: This statement describes the results of an experiment.

claim: FGF signaling does not just increase AMP number, but can also induce AMP spreading beyond the epithelial notum.
source: From this, we conclude that FGF signaling does not just increase AMP number, but can also induce AMP spreading beyond the epithelial notum.
evidence: This statement is a conclusion based on the experimental results.

claim: Ectopic pyr expression within the wing pouch using the TRiP-Overexpression VPR toolkit with a nub driver resulted in a large number of AMPs basal to the epithelium of the wing pouch.
source: To this end, we ectopically expressed pyr within the wing pouch using the TRiP-Overexpression VPR toolkit (Lin et al., 2015) with a nub driver. At the onset of nub expression, the pouch and the notum are separated by multiple cell diameters. We observed a large number of AMPs basal to the epithelium of the wing pouch (Figure 4C, D), suggesting that ectopic Pyr expression can even recruit AMPs from a distance of several cell diameters.
evidence: This statement describes the results of an experiment and is supported by reference to figures and a citation.

claim: Ectopic Pyr expression can recruit AMPs from a distance of several cell diameters.
source: We observed a large number of AMPs basal to the epithelium of the wing pouch (Figure 4C, D), suggesting that ectopic Pyr expression can even recruit AMPs from a distance of several cell diameters.
evidence: This statement is an inference based on the experimental results.

claim: AMPs throughout the A-P axis of the disc were found to be in both S- and M-phase of the cell cycle, as indicated by the incorporation of the thymidine analog EdU and staining for phospho-histone-H3 (PHH3).
source: To ascertain whether the AMPs were capable of proliferation at ectopic locations, we assessed whether the cells were progressing through the cell cycle. AMPs throughout the A-P axis of the disc were found to be in both S- and M-phase of the cell cycle, as indicated by the incorporation of the thymidine analog EdU and staining for phospho-histone-H3 (PHH3) (Figure 4E, F, Figure 4—figure supplement 1D, E).
